for r in claudinitewebsite crosswordchat edfringenow googlecalendareventcreator hitbut laughcounter missingbulbwebsite shepherd shoutsandwhispers tldr vascularcoloring wip; do
  rm -rf $r
  if timeout 90 git clone --depth 1 -q https://github.com/missingbulb/$r $r 2>/dev/null; then
    S=$r/.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml
    E=$r/.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml
    if [ ! -f "$S" ]; then echo "$r: NO scheduler workflow"; continue; fi
    thin=$(grep -c "github-script" "$S" "$E" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s}')
    mods=$(ls $r/.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/ 2>/dev/null | grep -cE "^(drain-dispatch|workflow-failure|executor-continuation)\.mjs$")
    pend=$(ls $r/.claudinite/pending-workflows/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    ver=$(grep -o '"engineVersion": *"[^"]*"' $r/.claudinite-settings.json 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.*: *"//;s/"//')
    echo "$r: github-script=$thin modules=$mods/3 pending=$pend engine=$ver"
  else
    echo "$r: CLONE FAILED"
  fi
done

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

* Hash every generated artifact, not the roster by name

The already-deployed gate hashed `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` because that
is what this deployment's roster happens to be called — but the roster's
file name is per-deployment config, and a member list that changed under a
different name would leave the site serving the old one. The glob is
over-inclusive by design: an extra rebuild costs one run, a missed one
costs a stale page.

Keeps this file identical to the pack's stub below its header.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/verify-in-production

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
```

No `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has already closed and
there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait. "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
  `.claudinite-settings.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or higher." "The live site's
  `/version.json` reports a version past 4.2.0." "Any session started after this landed — check
  the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge is not a
  production condition, and neither is elapsed time.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read an **unattended
  run can make**: an API response, a file at a URL, an issue's state. "Issue #100 on that repo
  is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check tidy-issues works". Only where no
  automatic check can exist may `Verify:` name a person's step, spelled out exactly.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it pushes `Not-before:` forward by exactly this much. Size it to the release you
  wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts. Beside it, in the body, **`Model: sonnet`** (reading a live artifact and judging an
assertion against it). Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to merge. If the mark
doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the next scheduler run.

## Tell the run how to converge

End the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole brief, and the run
decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the version, the value,
   the URL) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment
   saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking
   that; close this issue as completed — the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

Verified live on Shepherd: the thin scheduler workflow ran green (scheduler-run success, drain and report-failure correctly skipped). NOT yet exercised in production: drain-dispatch.mjs (needs a tick that leaves something pickable), workflow-failure.mjs (needs a failed run), executor-continuation.mjs (needs a dead executor run). input.title: Verify in production: the drain job actually runs drain-dispatch.mjs
input.body:
#1290 moved the scheduler workflow's drain from an inline `github-script` block to `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`. Unit tests cover the module, and the thin workflow itself has been watched running green on `missingbulb/Shepherd` ([run 32638669087](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32638669087)) — but on that run the queue was empty, so the `drain` job was **skipped by its own gate** and the new module has never actually executed inside a member's Actions job.

That is the one path worth proving live. It runs on every tick that leaves work pickable, and its failure mode is silent: the workflow parses, the run goes green, node exits on a bad path or a refused dispatch, and the queue simply stops draining. No test can answer whether the vendored path resolves and the job's token can fire the dispatch from inside a member repo — only a real run can.

(The two sibling modules, `workflow-failure.mjs` and `executor-continuation.mjs`, fire only when a run fails or dies. They cannot be forced without breaking something, and their unit coverage is the mechanism that comes back for them.)

Original-issue: #1289
In-production-when: `missingbulb/Shepherd` has a `claudinite-scheduler.yml` run created after 2026-08-23T12:11Z whose `drain` job has a conclusion of `success` (not `skipped`) — read the run's jobs, not the run's own conclusion, since the run is green either way.
Verify: that drain job's log shows the line `- dispatched the executor on <branch> to drain whatever this scheduler run created`, and a `claudinite-executor.yml` run of event `workflow_dispatch` exists in Shepherd within a few minutes after it. Pass = both. Fail = the drain job errored, or it succeeded with no matching executor run.
Not-before: 2026-08-24T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

Model: sonnet

---

### For the run

1. Read `In-production-when:` against Shepherd's real workflow runs. Never infer it from a merge, a green run, or elapsed time — a scheduler run whose `drain` job is `skipped` does **not** satisfy it; keep waiting.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the run URL, the drain job's log line and the matching executor run URL, then close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1289 with a comment saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by 1 day, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment.

content.text: Now the delivery gap the force exposed — that's a finding worth its own issue.

input.title: The fleet-baseline force lever cannot deliver an engine-only content change to an already-converged member
input.body:
Found while forcing #1290 across the fleet. The lever reported a clean sweep — **13 fired, 6 skipped, 0 failed** ([Shepherd run 32637790192](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32637790192)) — and **only 4 of the 13 actually took the change.** Eighteen minutes later the other 9 were still byte-identical to before; this is not a timing lag.

## Why

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.mjs`:

```js
if (stamp.convergedInWindow && !(signals.sharedMount?.changedPacks ?? []).length) {
  return { run: false, reason: 'the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due' };
}
```

and `engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`:

```js
const convergedInWindow = commits.some((c) => c.files.some((f) => f.startsWith(`${SHARED_SUBDIR}/`)));
```

#1290 is **engine-only** — it moved no `packs/` file, so no pack version moved. Every member that had already converged this morning has `convergedInWindow === true` and `changedPacks === []`, so the precondition correctly answers `run: false`. The wake re-queued the item, the executor re-evaluated at pick, and it declined. The members that *did* take it are the ones that happened to have a pack move pending.

Nothing here is behaving incorrectly. The gap is that **there is no same-day delivery path for an engine content change that bumps no `ENGINE_VERSION` and moves no pack** — and the force lever's report does not say so. This is exactly the "counts dispatches, not outcomes" blindness the task's own header warns about (Sheepdog#172): the sweep's own output reads as a successful fleet-wide delivery.

## Observed

| Took #1290 | Declined |
|---|---|
| `claudinitecanary`, `shepherd`, `shoutsandwhispers`, `wip` | `crosswordchat`, `edfringenow`, `googlecalendareventcreator`, `hitbut`, `laughcounter`, `tldr`, `vascularcoloring` |

(`claudinitewebsite` and `missingbulbwebsite` were fired but could not be cloned to check.)

The 9 will converge at their next window, when `convergedInWindow` goes false — within ~24h. So this is a latency gap, not a correctness one. But it is a latency gap that silently defeats the one lever built to close it.

## Worth deciding

- Should `fleet-baseline` report **outcomes** rather than dispatches — i.e. read each member's stamp or mount after firing, so a sweep that delivered to 4 of 13 says so? That is the fix that makes the lever honest regardless of cause.
- Should the `update` precondition consider canon HEAD's own movement (`stamp.canonHead` is already collected) and not just pack versions, so an engine content change is "due"?
- Or is the answer simply that an engine change that must reach the fleet today has to bump `ENGINE_VERSION` — in which case that belongs written down where a session forcing a change will read it.

I have not picked one; each trades differently and the third is a standing-decision question.

content.text: {"id":"5226825103","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1292"}

Fleet forced and verified. Here's what actually happened, including the part that didn't go as my PR body claimed.

**It works.** The thin scheduler workflow ran green in production on Shepherd — [run 32638669087](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32638669087): `scheduler-run` succeeded on the new shape, `drain` and `report-failure` each correctly skipped by their own gates. And on `claudinitecanary` the delivery is complete end-to-end: all three new modules vendored, both workflows in the thin shape with zero `github-script`, nothing left staged in `pending-workflows/`, cron correctly resolved to its own hashed minute.

**But the force only reached 4 of 13.** The lever reported `13 fired, 6 skipped, 0 failed` — a clean sweep. It wasn't one. Eighteen minutes later, 9 members were byte-identical to before.

The cause is not a bug, and I checked it rather than guessed: `update`'s precondition declines when `stamp.convergedInWindow && !changedPacks.length`. #1290 is engine-only — no `packs/` file moved, so no pack version moved — and every member that converged this morning correctly answered "nothing due." The 4 that took it happened to have a pack move pending. The other 9 arrive at their next window, within ~24h.

So my PR body's claim that forcing would deliver this fleet-wide was wrong, and I've filed the gap rather than papered over it:

- [#1292](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1292) — the force lever can't deliver an engine-only change to an already-converged member, **and its report doesn't say so**. Three candidate fixes laid out; I picked none, because one of them is a standing-decision call for you.
- [#1291](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1291) — verify-in-production, sub-issue of #1289: `drain-dispatch.mjs` has still never executed inside a member's Actions job, because every run I could force had an empty queue and the gate skipped it. That's the one module whose failure would be silent (green run, queue quietly stops draining), so it waits on a real drain firing on Shepherd. Retries daily from tomorrow 06:00Z.

`workflow-failure.mjs` and `executor-continuation.mjs` fire only on a failed or dead run. I can't force those without breaking something, so their unit coverage stands as the mechanism.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> - **[#1292](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1292)** needs your call — should `fleet-baseline` report outcomes instead of dispatches, should `update` gate on canon HEAD moving, or is "bump `ENGINE_VERSION` to reach the fleet today" the rule to write down?
> - **[#1291](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1291)** is queued and self-retrying; no action from you.
> - 9 members converge onto the thin workflows on their own next anchor, ~24h.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.

- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. - file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. - repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. - single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. - verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.

options.label: Deferred outcome item (Recommended)
options.description: The sweep fires, records each member's pre-dispatch settings-file sha, and files ONE follow-up work item on the existing do-later lane with Not-before +30min carrying that table. No run ever sleeps, the #649 retirement of the follow stands, and the outcome report is accurate because it looks after the dust settles. Cost: the answer arrives in a second artifact, ~30min later.

One artifact, answer immediately. Cost: it is a shorter version of the follow #649 retired, and it will under-report any member whose update PR merges after the settle — in my run, several took 5-10 minutes, so some would read as 'did not move' when they were about to.

options.label: Report readiness, not outcomes
options.description: Don't chase the outcome at all. Instead make the report say what the dispatch could NOT do: for each member, print its current stamp and whether its mount already converged today, so the reader sees up front which members a wake will find nothing due on. Free (the sweep already reads the declaration), no new machinery, and it would have surfaced my 9 laggards — but it reports a prediction, not what actually happened.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: fleet-baseline: follow every member to current, and report outcomes rather than dispatches
input.body:
Owner decision, reversing #649's "give up the follow": `fleet-baseline` must answer, in the run that fires it, **whether every covered member ended at the freshest engine and pack versions the published catalog names** — not merely that a dispatch was accepted.

Today the sweep reports `fired / skipped / failed` where `fired` means "the dispatch POST returned 204". #1292 recorded what that costs: a sweep reported `13 fired, 0 failed` while 9 of the 13 took nothing.

## What it must report, per member

1. **dispatched** — the 204 (what it reports today).
2. **started** — a `claudinite-scheduler.yml` run of event `workflow_dispatch` appeared at or after the dispatch instant.
3. **current** — the member's `.claudinite-settings.json` stamps the engine and every declared pack at the versions canon publishes.

A member that was **already current before the dispatch** is a success, distinguished in the report from one that **converged** during the run: its update correctly declines, and demanding work of it would be reporting a fault where there is none.

## Reuse, don't rewrite

`tasks/fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs` in this same pack already carries both halves of the comparison — `canonVersions(gh, canonRepo)` reads canon's `ENGINE_VERSION` and each `packs/<id>/pack.mjs` version over the API, and `classifyFreshness({ hasScheduler, installed, canon })` returns `fresh` or `behind` with the gap spelled out. The follow imports those rather than growing a second implementation.

## Not a return of the 45-minute sleep

#649 retired the follow because it was a blind fixed wait that forced the lever to be a standalone workflow. What lands here is a **bounded poll on a real terminal condition** — each member exits the loop the moment it reads current, and the loop ends when all of them have or the budget expires. A quiet fleet where everything is already current terminates in one pass, in seconds.

## Known limitation, to be stated in the report itself

Freshness is judged by **published version numbers**, which is what the owner asked for. Engine or pack *content* shipped without a version bump is therefore invisible to this check — a member can read `current` while lacking the newest commit. That is exactly the case #1292 found, and the report must say so rather than imply content-level currency.

Closes #1292's first option; leaves its other two open questions moot.

# Fleet baseline — force every member to baseline now

**This task runs no agent, and no schedule.** It is `frequency: manual` with `agent_model: none`: the scheduler run never instantiates it, and the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) → [`force-fleet-baseline.mjs`](force-fleet-baseline.mjs) the executor runs as code-work when — and only when — a human creates an item for it. This file is the human-facing record of what that is; there is no agent phase.

## How to pull the lever

Create the work item, from a checkout of this repo with `GITHUB_TOKEN` set:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/create-work-item.mjs claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-baseline \
  --context "REPOS=Alpha Beta" \
  --context "DRY_RUN=true" \
  --context "INCLUDE_DORMANT=true"
```

Every `--context` line is optional:

```
REPOS=Alpha Beta            ← limit to these repos (bare name or owner/name, SPACE-separated); omit for every covered member
DRY_RUN=true                ← report what would fire, fire nothing
INCLUDE_DORMANT=true        ← dormant members are skipped by default — they stopped their own scheduler on purpose
```

Values are space-separated because the parameter bag splits `KEY=value` pairs on commas. The two safety knobs are read from the item's Context and from nowhere else: an item created without them runs unscoped and live.

## What it does

Enumerate every repo under the configured owner over the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT and, for each **covered, non-dormant** member, dispatch that member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with `wake: update` — the same button the owner would press in that repo's Actions tab, pressed across the fleet in one run. The wake lever names one task, so each member does exactly one thing: converge its mount.

Nothing is baselined *here*, and nothing is written to any member — no commit, no issue, no comment. Each member converges its own mount, with its own token, under its own scheduler and delivery policy; if its converge needs an agent, that member's own executor runs it. The enforcer **dispatches**; the member **executes**. That is the whole trust model: no agent anywhere needs cross-repo access, and the one fleet credential is the PAT with Actions write.

Every repo under the owner lands in the run summary under exactly one state — fired, canon, out-of-scope, excluded, filtered-out, uncovered, dormant, or failed — so a fleet-wide force is never mistaken for fleet-wide coverage.

## What it deliberately does not do

**It does not wait.** A dispatch queues a run; what that run went on to do is each member's own story, told where members always tell it — a maintenance PR, a work item, a failure escalation in that repo. The retired workflow's *follow* half (watch every member to a terminal state, render a fleet report) is what forced the lever to be a standalone workflow with a 45-minute sleep; giving it up is what lets the lever ride the ordinary scheduler. If a member's forced run went wrong, that member says so in its own repo.

## Why a task and not a workflow (any more)

The standalone `fleet-baseline.yml` workflow (retired 2026-08-11, #749) lived in the enforcer's `.github/` — the one place the nightly converge can never push (#649), so every change to it crossed the fleet by the slow withhold-and-hand-to-the-agent path. As a task, the lever ships with the ordinary vendor refresh like everything else, and the repo's vendored scheduler stays its **only** workflow. The typed `workflow_dispatch` inputs the old workflow offered are carried by the item's Context above.

## Failure is loud

A member that could not be dispatched — a missing scheduler workflow, a PAT without Actions write, a workflow GitHub disabled — is named in the summary under `failed`, and the sweep exits non-zero. The executor converges the item to `needs-human`, so a broken grant escalates rather than silently leaving part of the fleet unforced.

input.body:
Closes #1293

## The problem

A dispatch POST returning 204 says a run was **queued** and nothing more. A report built from those 204s describes the sweep's own outgoing calls while reading as fleet-wide delivery. #1292 recorded the cost: a run announced `13 fired, 0 failed` while 9 of the 13 took nothing.

## What it does now

After firing, the sweep follows each dispatched member until a terminal condition read **off the member itself** — does its own `.claudinite-settings.json` stamp the engine and every declared pack at the versions canon publishes?

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `converged` | was behind canon, reached its versions during this run |
| `already-current` | was at canon's versions before the dispatch, so its update correctly declined |
| `did-not-converge` | its scheduler ran and it is still behind — go and read it |
| `never-started` | the dispatch was accepted and no run followed it |
| `unknown` | the member could not be read |

The headline becomes **`current of dispatched`**, and the run **fails** when a dispatched member never got there — the case the old report counted as a win.

`already-current` is a success in its own right, and a distinct one. Such a member's `update` precondition correctly declines and it does no work; folding it into a failure would report a fault where there is none, and into `converged` would claim work that did not happen. Reading it requires a freshness probe *before* the dispatch, which is where that read now happens.

## Reuse, not reimplementation

`canonVersions` and `classifyFreshness` already existed in this pack for the roster's drift issues. They are imported, not copied — same pack, so no cross-pack dependency.

## This is not #649's sleep coming back

That follow was a **blind fixed wait** every run paid whatever the fleet was doing, and it forced the lever to be a standalone workflow with a `.github/` managed copy. `follow-to-current.mjs` polls a **real terminal condition** and each member leaves the loop the moment it reads current — an already-current fleet finishes on the first pass in seconds, and the lever stays an ordinary queue task.

`code_work_timeout` rises 900s → 1800s so the 20-minute follow budget (`FOLLOW_MINUTES`, overridable per item) finishes well inside it. A run the platform kills never prints the report it spent the time earning, and there's a test asserting that margin holds.

## The limitation, stated in the report itself

"Current" is a claim about **published version numbers**. Canon content shipped without a version bump moves no number, so a member can read `already-current` while lacking canon's newest commit — exactly the #1292 case. The report says this in its own words rather than letting the word imply more than was checked.

## Purging the reversed decision

The old "it does not wait" is written down in several places, and all of them are now wrong. Removed from the pack `RULES.md`, both `README.md`s, and the task test literally named *"…and never follows"* — replaced there by a test of the bound that makes the follow safe.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2708 pass, 0 fail**. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking. `check_the_work`: clean.
- 19 new tests, clock and sleep injected so nothing waits.
- See-it-fail on every new assertion: collapsing `already-current` into `converged`, treating a timed-out member as success, dropping the never-started distinction, reverting the headline to a dispatch count, removing the follow-failure escalation, and dropping the limitation note — each went red, then green.

**Not yet exercised against the real fleet.** I can drive it once merged, which is also the honest test of whether the 20-minute budget matches what members actually take.

Two things worth your attention.

The distinction that makes this honest is **`already-current` as its own success**. Those 9 members from this morning weren't failures — they were at canon's published versions and their `update` correctly declined. The old report couldn't say that, and neither could a naive "did it move?" check; it needs a freshness read taken *before* the dispatch, which is why that read moved earlier in the sweep.

And the limitation is printed in the report itself: *current* means published version numbers. My #1290 shipped engine content with no version bump, so those members would still read `already-current` while lacking it. The lever now tells the truth about what it checked rather than letting the word carry more than it earned.

I didn't touch the `update` precondition or the other two options in #1292 — you picked this one, and it makes the lever honest regardless of why a member declines.

> - **Not yet run against the real fleet** — I can drive it once merged, which is also the only real test of whether 20 minutes matches what members actually take.
> - **[#1291](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1291)** still queued: `drain-dispatch.mjs` has yet to execute in a member's Actions job.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.

- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.

- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
